picks.intervention_label: GFH375 / VS-7375, KRAS G12D(ON/OFF)-selective inhibitor (VS-7375 + cetuximab, 1L PDAC cohort, NCT07644559)
picks.rationale: This is the exact allele on the exact target, and the response rate is the loudest signal in the whole dossier: 41% confirmed ORR (90% CI 30-52) with 97% disease control in pretreated G12D PDAC. The upside I am chasing is that a 1L, chemo-sparing oral drug reproduces or beats that in a treatment-naive tumor, where response fractions in this disease usually run in the teens. The efficacy read is second-line and single-arm so it is not proof, and mPFS was only 5.52 months, but for a 79-year-old who would otherwise face FOLFIRINOX I want the allele-matched shot on goal first.
primary_concerns: ORR and mPFS come from previously-treated patients; the treatment-naive 1L number is unknown and could regress
grade >=3 TRAE 30% with neutropenia and anemia, and the cetuximab pairing adds a rash/hypomagnesemia burden that a 79-year-old may tolerate poorly
durability is thin at 5.52-month mPFS, so acquired resistance may arrive fast

picks.intervention_label: HRS-4642 (KRAS G12D inhibitor) + gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel, first-line (phase 3 NCT07232875; phase 1b/2 Nat Med)
picks.rationale: The front-line combination hit a 63.3% ORR (95% CI 43.9-80.1) in 30 treatment-naive G12D PDAC patients, which is roughly double what gem/nab-paclitaxel alone delivers and the single most striking 1L number I found. If that holds, layering an allele-matched inhibitor onto a standard backbone is exactly the kind of high-ceiling move worth taking early. The catch is a 90.3% grade >=3 TRAE rate driven by the chemo backbone, and the phase 3 is not-yet-recruiting, so this may be an intent-to-enroll rather than a today slot.
primary_concerns: 90.3% grade >=3 TRAE, largely hematologic, is a real problem at age 79 with an assumed rather than measured ECOG
n=30 for the efficacy readout is small and PFS/OS were not reported, so the ORR could be a soft surrogate
the phase 3 is not yet recruiting, so timing may not match the patient's window

picks.intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor, first-line (RASolute 303, NCT07491445)
picks.rationale: This is the one option with randomized survival data behind it: RASolute 302 showed OS HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.30-0.53) with median OS 13.2 vs 6.7 months and grade >=3 toxicity actually lower than chemotherapy. Even though it is pan-RAS rather than G12D-selective, it covers G12D, and the enrollable 1L RASolute 303 randomizes against gem/nab-paclitaxel, so the downside is capped by an active comparator. I rank it below the selective agents only because I am hunting for the higher response ceiling, but this is the pick with the firmest floor.
primary_concerns: pan-RAS mechanism hits wild-type RAS too, so the rash/stomatitis skin-mucosal burden is characteristic and near-universal at any grade
the OS anchor is second-line; the 1L readout is not yet mature
randomization in RASolute 303 means a chance of assignment to the chemo-only arm

picks.intervention_label: INCB161734, KRAS G12D-selective inhibitor (1L parent NCT06179160; phase 3 DAWN-303 NCT07522073)
picks.rationale: A second sponsor's allele-matched agent with a 37% monotherapy ORR and 78% DCR in heavily pretreated G12D PDAC, and notably the monotherapy toxicity was GI-only with rash and stomatitis absent, which is a cleaner profile than the pan-RAS skin signature. The upside is a G12D-selective oral drug that spares the mucosal toxicity while still delivering a high response fraction, with 1L combination cohorts already open. It sits behind the top picks only because the response data are second-line-plus and the enrollable chemo-combination cohort carries ~40% grade >=3 neutropenia.
primary_concerns: 37% ORR is from patients with >=2 prior lines; the 1L number is untested
the gem/nab-paclitaxel combination cohort ran ~40% grade >=3 neutropenia
PFS and DoR were not reached at ~5 months, so durability is unquantified

picks.intervention_label: zoldonrasib (RMC-9805), KRAS G12D(ON)-selective inhibitor, first-line (RASolute 305, NCT07621718)
picks.rationale: The G12D(ON)-selective RAS(ON) agent that maps to the patient's exact allele, with a 30% ORR and 80% DCR and, importantly, a well-tolerated profile at 1200 mg/day with no grade 4-5 treatment-related events. The bet is that pairing a clean-tolerability selective inhibitor with chemotherapy in the double-blind 1L RASolute 305 gives durable disease control in an older patient who cannot absorb much toxicity. It ranks last of the KRAS agents only because its 30% ORR trails the 37-41% seen with INCB161734 and GFH375, not because of any safety concern.
primary_concerns: ORR 30% is the lowest of the selective agents and PFS/DoR were not reported in the abstract
RASolute 305 is placebo-plus-chemo controlled, so there is a chance of assignment to chemo alone
the response data are second-line, so the 1L signal is inferred not observed

notes: Treatment-naive metastatic PDAC, KRAS G12D confirmed on ctDNA, ECOG 1 assumed at age 79. My prior pushes the allele-matched G12D-selective agents with the loudest single-arm ORR to the top (GFH375 41%, HRS-4642+chemo 63%, INCB161734 37%), even though every one of those numbers comes from previously-treated patients and none has mature PFS/OS. I keep daraxonrasib at rank 3 rather than lower because it is the only intervention with a randomized OS HR (0.40) and an enrollable 1L slot with an active comparator, which is the firmest floor on the board. I deliberately left the ARID1A/ATR axis (ceralasertib) and the KRAS vaccines off my ranked picks: the ATR read is cross-tumor with no PDAC responder and gated on BAF250a IHC, and every enrollable vaccine option is adjuvant/maintenance or ECOG-0-gated, so none clears my upside bar for this metastatic patient right now. Tissue NGS confirmation of the ctDNA G12D call is the shared enrollment token across all five picks.

picks.intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor — front-line via RASolute 303 (NCT07491445)
picks.rationale: Of everything on the KRAS axis this is the only agent with a randomized phase 3 readout and a per-term grade >=3 table I can actually plan around: RASolute 302 gave OS HR 0.40 in the RAS G12 stratum, and the drug's grade >=3 TRAE rate ran 43.6% against 57.5% on chemotherapy, so the toxicity trades under the comparator rather than adding to it. The G3+ burden is skin and mucosa — rash 14%, stomatitis 12% — both of which have settled dermatologic and oral-care management algorithms, and TRAE-driven discontinuation was 1.2% versus 11.2% on chemo. Follow-up is still short by post-marketing standards (2L pivotal cut in 2026, no 5-year safety) and the front-line RASolute 303 slot is investigational, so I hold at moderate. For a 79-year-old this is the least-surprising toxicity profile in the option set.
primary_concerns: No long-term (>=5 yr) safety follow-up; the pivotal data are 2L and read across to the treatment-naive 1L slot rather than being generated in it
Any-grade rash approaches 91% in the phase 1/2 PDAC set — low-grade but near-universal, and dose modification ran ~48%, which matters for adherence in an older patient

RASolute 303 randomizes to monotherapy, mono+chemo, or chemo; the mono+chemo arm layers the daraxonrasib rash onto chemo myelosuppression, a combination without its own dedicated safety characterization

picks.intervention_label: zoldonrasib (RMC-9805) + chemotherapy — front-line via RASolute 305 (NCT07621718)
picks.rationale: Zoldonrasib maps to the exact G12D allele and carries the cleanest single-agent tolerability signal I have: phase 1 at 1200 mg/day showed no grade 4 or 5 treatment-related events, GI toxicity that stayed grade 1-2 (nausea 27%, diarrhea 20%), and only a 1% grade 3 ALT rise. The catch is maturity — that read is an ASCO GI 2025 abstract, n=40, with PFS and DoR not reported, so the drug-specific long-tail is genuinely unknown. The enrollable front-line RASolute 305 adds it to mFOLFIRINOX or gem/nab-paclitaxel against placebo+chemo, which means the incremental grade >=3 burden the patient takes on is the known chemotherapy backbone rather than a novel signature. I rank it second, not first, because the phase 3 efficacy is unproven and the safety base is 40 patients deep.
primary_concerns: Safety base is a single 40-patient phase 1 abstract; no mature grade >=3 union rate or per-term G3+ breakdown published yet

The placebo-controlled design keeps the chemo backbone honest, but a treatment-naive 79-year-old still absorbs full-intensity mFOLFIRINOX or gem/nab-paclitaxel toxicity on top of the investigational agent
Efficacy for the combination is not yet demonstrated — the front-line survival benefit is a hypothesis built on a 30% single-agent ORR

picks.intervention_label: INCB161734 (KRAS G12D-selective) + chemotherapy — front-line via DAWN-303 (NCT07522073)
picks.rationale: The monotherapy AE picture is the reason this ranks above the other combination agents: phase 1 GI toxicity ran 50-60% but stayed grade 1-2, and rash and stomatitis were notably absent, so it does not stack skin toxicity onto a chemo backbone the way the pan-RAS agents do. The grade >=3 neutropenia (~40%) clustered in the chemo-combination cohort and reads as chemo-driven, with no treatment-related deaths. DAWN-303 is a randomized double-blind chemo +/- INCB161734 design, so the added-agent toxicity is measured against placebo+chemo rather than assumed. Confidence is moderate-to-low: the supporting efficacy is a 37% ORR in a heavily pretreated single-arm set (n=41), and the neutropenia rate in combination warrants an explicit growth-factor and monitoring plan before I would call it managed in a 79-year-old.
primary_concerns: ~40% grade >=3 neutropenia in the chemo-combination cohort needs a defined growth-factor/monitoring algorithm; in a 79-year-old this is the load-bearing safety question, not the agent's own low-grade GI profile
Efficacy anchor is single-arm, pretreated, n=41 (ORR 37%); the front-line survival case is extrapolated
Retifanlimab-containing cohorts exist in the parent phase 1 — an anti-PD-1 pairing I would not endorse given MSS/TMB 8.6, where checkpoint benefit is low and irAE risk is not offset

picks.intervention_label: GFH375 / VS-7375 (KRAS G12D-selective) + cetuximab — front-line via NCT07644559
picks.rationale: This is the G12D-selective agent with the most quantified toxicity table after daraxonrasib: ESMO 2025 gave grade >=3 TRAE 30.3% (one grade 4 neutropenia), with a myelosuppression-plus-GI signature — neutrophils decreased 49% any-grade / 8% grade >=3, anemia 42% / 8% grade >=3, diarrhea 56% / 3% grade >=3 — and no dose-limiting toxicities at 600 mg. The cytopenias have standard management algorithms, which is why it clears my bar for a ranked slot. What drops it to fourth is the cetuximab pairing in the 1L cohort: cetuximab adds its own well-known acneiform rash, hypomagnesemia, and infusion-reaction burden, and the doublet has no dedicated combination safety characterization in PDAC. The efficacy base is also one line beyond this patient (previously-treated, ORR 41%).
primary_concerns: Myelosuppression is real (neutrophils 8% and anemia 8% at grade >=3) and the cetuximab partner adds a separate, uncharacterized-in-combination toxicity layer for PDAC
Single-arm efficacy sits at 2L+ (ORR 41%, mPFS 5.52 mo); the 1L benefit is unproven
China-only phase 1/2 data; population and supportive-care context may not transfer directly to a US 79-year-old

picks.intervention_label: ceralasertib (AZD6738), ATR inhibitor — ARID1A-stratified basket (NCT03682289)
picks.rationale: I carry the ARID1A synthetic-lethal axis at rank 5 rather than any pan-KRAS or checkpoint-vaccine option because the ATR-inhibitor class has a well-characterized and manageable toxicity — cytopenias (anemia, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia) with established dose-hold and transfusion algorithms, and no treatment-related deaths in the ARID1A-deficient phase 2. The efficacy is honestly weak for this tumor: 14% ORR across the full ARID1A-deficient set, with activity concentrating in gynecologic histologies and the non-gynecologic (PDAC-relevant) signal thinner. This slot is conditional: entry gates on BAF250a/ARID1A protein loss by IHC, and only ~two-thirds of ARID1A-mutant tumors show that loss, so the ctDNA frameshift call alone does not confirm eligibility. I would not move on it until IHC confirms loss and the treating team has a chemotherapy backbone decided.
primary_concerns: PDAC-relevant efficacy is weak — 14% ORR overall, activity skewed to gynecologic tumors

Per-term grade >=3 cytopenia rates were not broken out in the abstract, so the class signature is known but the trial-specific G3+ magnitude is not; the ATR class reference (camonsertib grade 3 anemia ~26%) sets expectations
Eligibility is IHC-gated on BAF250a loss; without confirmed protein loss the frameshift call does not secure a slot

notes: Full option set re-scored after the 9 new on-axis rows. Deliberately NOT ranked, with the specific missing safety datum named for each: (1) pan-KRAS BBO-11818, BLU-924, PF-07934040 — all tier 5 with empty toxicities[] and no published per-term grade >=3 table; I cannot rank an agent whose grade >=3 union rate does not yet exist, and I am declining to rank on novelty-of-mechanism grounds specifically because the AE quantification is absent, not because the mechanism is new. (2) HRS-4642 + gem/nab-paclitaxel (NCT07232875, 1L phase 3) — deliberately excluded from the top 5 despite a 63.3% ORR because grade >=3 TRAE ran 90.3%; even read as chemo-backbone-driven, a 90.3% G3+ rate in a 79-year-old is a tolerability profile I will not top-rank, and HRS-4642 monotherapy additionally carries a metabolic signature (hypertriglyceridemia, hypercholesterolemia) plus one treatment-related death (1/84). Flagging HRS-4642+chemo as a likely round-2 toxicity-dissent candidate if another persona ranks it first. (3) KRAS vaccines — ELI-002 has the cleanest safety in the whole dossier (no grade >=3, all grade 1-2) but sits in the adjuvant/MRD setting, a setting mismatch for unresectable metastatic disease; the mKRAS+nivo/ipi and balstilimab/botensilimab constructs add dual-checkpoint immune toxicity with NO per-term irAE breakout, and that uncharacterized G3+ irAE rate in an unselected 79-year-old is the decision-relevant gap. Cross-cutting: MSS/TMB 8.6 makes any anti-PD-1-containing arm low-yield, so the checkpoint pairings carry irAE risk without a commensurate efficacy rationale here. Assumptions inherited from intake (ECOG 1, treatment-naive, US, efficacy/toxicity weight 0.5) flagged; at age 79 a more toxicity-averse weight would push zoldonrasib+chemo and the daraxonrasib monotherapy arm up relative to any chemo-doublet.

picks.intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor
picks.rationale: One intervention on this board clears the bar I actually hold: RASolute 302 is a randomized phase 3 (n=500) with a pre-specified OS primary endpoint hit at HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.30-0.53, p=4.6e-11), published in NEJM, and the RAS G12 stratum that contains G12D holds the effect at HR 0.40 (CI 0.30-0.54). That is registration-grade, not a signal. Two honest caveats keep me from calling it settled: the trial is open-label, so PFS and ORR carry detection bias (OS is largely immune to it, which is why I lean on the OS number), and the pivotal data are 2L while the enrollable slot for a treatment-naive patient is 1L RASolute 303 (NCT07491445), which has not read out. The 1L benefit is a cross-line inference, not yet demonstrated, but the mechanism and the 2L magnitude make this the defensible lead.
primary_concerns: RoB2 domain 4 (measurement of outcome): open-label design biases PFS/ORR ascertainment; I weight OS, which the design does not compromise
directness/applicability: registration efficacy is 2L, the 1L RASolute 303 slot is unread, so front-line benefit is extrapolated across line not proven
pan-RAS rather than G12D-selective, so target coverage is broader than the allele but the allele-specific contribution is not isolable from this trial

picks.intervention_label: zoldonrasib (RMC-9805), KRAS G12D(ON)-selective inhibitor
picks.rationale: This is the one place I credit biology over data: it hits G12D directly, which is a cleaner target rationale than daraxonrasib's pan-RAS extrapolation. But the clinical read is a single-arm phase 1 abstract, n=40, ORR 30% with no reported confidence interval and no PFS or DoR, so what I have is an unreplicated surrogate endpoint from a conference abstract, not a durability estimate. The front-line RASolute 305 (NCT07621718) is a registered double-blind phase 3, which is the correct design to settle this, but it has produced no readout yet, so ranking it here rests on the allele match plus a promising-but-immature response rate. I put it second because the target fit is genuine, not because the evidence is.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I: single-arm, no comparator, so the 30% ORR has no control to net against and no CI to bound it
surrogate-only endpoint: PFS and DoR were not reported in the ASCO GI abstract, so durability is unknown
abstract-stage reporting, not a peer-reviewed full paper; I have not seen the RoB profile of the primary analysis

picks.intervention_label: GFH375 / VS-7375, oral KRAS G12D(ON/OFF)-selective inhibitor
picks.rationale: The highest single-arm response number for an allele-matched agent here, ORR 41% (90% CI 30-52) in 59 evaluable previously-treated G12D PDAC, with mPFS 5.52 mo. Two things temper it and I will name both: it is a single-country study (GFH375X1101, China) reported as an ESMO abstract, so geographic generalizability to a US population and full-manuscript RoB are both open questions, and the interval is a 90% CI, a wider alpha than the 95% I would want quoted. The randomized phase 3 against chemotherapy (NCT07262567) is the design that would actually test this, but it sits at 2L and has no readout, so for a treatment-naive patient this is evidence one line removed. I rank it below zoldonrasib only because zoldonrasib carries a registered 1L phase 3 in progress; on response magnitude alone GFH375 is the stronger single-arm number.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I:Moderate single-arm; ORR reported with a 90% (not 95%) CI and no comparator arm
geographic generalizability: single-country (China) phase 1/2, US applicability untested
directness: evaluable efficacy is 2L+ (68% had >=2 prior lines), the patient is treatment-naive, so the 1L cohort of NCT07644559 is the fit but has no efficacy read

picks.intervention_label: HRS-4642 (KRAS G12D inhibitor) + gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel, front-line
picks.rationale: This is the only allele-directed agent with front-line data at the patient's exact line, ORR 63.3% (95% CI 43.9-80.1) in 30 treatment-naive patients, peer-reviewed in Nature Medicine. The single-arm design is the problem I cannot get past: 63% ORR is measured on top of a gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone that delivers roughly 20-23% ORR on its own, so without a control arm I cannot apportion how much is the drug, and the HRS-4642 monotherapy read was only 20.8% ORR, which is the honest ceiling on its independent contribution. Grade >=3 TRAEs ran 90.3%, driven by the chemo backbone, and this is a China-based study with the confirmatory phase 3 (NCT07232875) not yet recruiting. I rank it fourth because the setting fit is exact but the attributable effect is confounded and the toxicity is heavy for a 79-year-old.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I: single-arm, so the 63.3% combination ORR is confounded with the chemo backbone and not attributable to HRS-4642; monotherapy ORR was only 20.8%
grade >=3 TRAE 90.3% (backbone-driven) is a marrow-reserve concern at age 79
geographic generalizability (China) plus a confirmatory phase 3 that is not yet recruiting; no randomized evidence exists

picks.intervention_label: ceralasertib (AZD6738), ATR inhibitor (ARID1A synthetic-lethal axis)
picks.rationale: I keep this on the list as a mechanistically independent second axis, not because the in-indication evidence supports it. The phase 2 (NCT03682289, n=29) returned 14% ORR across the full ARID1A-deficient population, and every response clustered in gynecologic histology; there is no PDAC responder in the data, so the pancreatic case is pure cross-tumor extrapolation. Enrollment is gated on BAF250a IHC loss, and only about two-thirds of ARID1A-mutant tumors show protein loss, so the frameshift call alone does not confirm eligibility. It ranks last on the evidence: a banked axis worth validating with IHC, but the current PDAC signal is absent, not merely weak.
primary_concerns: no PDAC responder in the clinical ARID1A data; case_match is cross_tumor_only, so PDAC activity is extrapolated
eligibility depends on BAF250a IHC loss that the frameshift does not reliably predict (~67% concordance), so the patient may screen-fail the target
class ATR-inhibitor cytopenias (anemia in particular) are dose-limiting and matter more at 79

notes: I did not abstain because daraxonrasib alone gives the board one genuinely RCT-grade option, which is more than many dossiers offer. The gap between rank 1 and everything below it is large and I want that on the record: RASolute 302 is a registered phase-3 OS hit, while ranks 2-5 are single-arm phase-1/2 surrogate-endpoint reads (zoldonrasib, GFH375, HRS-4642) or a cross-tumor extrapolation with no in-indication responder (ceralasertib). I deliberately left the pan-KRAS FIH agents (BBO-11818, BLU-924, PF-07934040) and LY3962673 off the ranking entirely: they are pre-data, tier-5, with no efficacy denominator, so ranking them would be ranking a mechanism, not evidence. The KRAS vaccine and TCR-T axes are also off: NT-112 and the C*08:02 TCR-T are HLA-mismatched (he is C*05:01/C*06:02), and ELI-002 plus the Hopkins nivo/ipi vaccine only carry adjuvant/MRD data where, critically, the efficacy split is by on-treatment immune response rather than randomization (ROBINS-I:Serious, immortal-time/responder bias), so those numbers cannot be read as metastatic efficacy. Checkpoint monotherapy stays out on MSS and TMB 8.6. Two evidence-integrity flags for the board: the GFH375 and HRS-4642 reads are single-country (China) and the HRS-4642 Nat Med paper has no PubMed record yet (cited by DOI), which I have not independently verified beyond the reference-check note. ECOG 1 is assumed; a worse performance status would harden my concern about the 90% G3+ HRS-4642 combination.

picks.intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor — RASolute 303 first-line (NCT07491445)
picks.rationale: No KRAS G12D therapy is approved, so NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2025 puts a newly diagnosed metastatic patient on comprehensive somatic and germline profiling plus clinical-trial enrollment; there is no consensus category to assign, and this is the guideline-consonant route rather than an off-guideline gamble. Of the enrollable trials, daraxonrasib has by far the strongest controlled evidence: RASolute 302 read out an OS HR of 0.40 (95% CI 0.30-0.53) in the RAS G12 stratum that carries his G12D (pmid:42223072), and it holds FDA breakthrough designation, which is the nearest thing to cross-body agreement this axis has before approval. RASolute 303 (NCT07491445) opens the matching first-line slot for a treatment-naive ECOG-1 patient.
primary_concerns: The randomized phase-3 evidence sits at second line; first-line benefit is inferred from RASolute 303's design, not yet demonstrated.
The G12D call is plasma ctDNA — tissue NGS confirmation is the enrollment token the RAS(ON) protocols expect.
RASolute 303 randomizes against gem/nab-paclitaxel, so an assigned patient may draw the chemo control arm rather than the drug.

picks.intervention_label: zoldonrasib (RMC-9805), KRAS G12D(ON)-selective inhibitor — RASolute 305 first-line (NCT07621718)
picks.rationale: Zoldonrasib maps to his exact allele, and RASolute 305 (NCT07621718) requires KRAS G12D and enrolls treatment-naive metastatic PDAC, so it matches him on allele, tumor type, and line. As a trial it is guideline-consonant under NCCN Pancreatic v2.2025, with no consensus category yet since the agent is investigational and the front-line efficacy read is still open. The phase-1 signal (ORR 30%, DCR 80%, doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.4_suppl.724) is thinner than daraxonrasib's randomized data, which is why it sits second.
primary_concerns: The efficacy base is a single-arm phase-1 abstract with no mature PFS or DoR; the first-line phase 3 has not read out.
RASolute 305 randomizes against placebo plus mFOLFIRINOX or gem/nab-paclitaxel, and mFOLFIRINOX is a demanding backbone in a patient this age.
Tissue-documented G12D is required for entry.

picks.intervention_label: INCB161734, KRAS G12D-selective inhibitor + chemotherapy — DAWN-303 first-line (NCT07522073)
picks.rationale: DAWN-303 (NCT07522073) requires KRAS G12D and enrolls previously untreated metastatic PDAC, so it fits his allele, tumor type, and line, and adds a second sponsor to the front-line G12D field. It is guideline-consonant as a trial under NCCN Pancreatic v2.2025, again with no consensus category. The phase-1 monotherapy read is the strongest single-agent G12D-PDAC response surfaced here (ORR 37%, DCR 78%, doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.2_suppl.654), which is what motivates the front-line combination test.
primary_concerns: Phase-1 population was heavily pretreated (>=2 prior lines); extrapolating that response to first line is an assumption.
Grade >=3 neutropenia clustered around 40% in the chemo-combination cohort, which matters more in a 79-year-old on a chemo backbone.
No mature PFS or randomized comparison yet.

picks.intervention_label: VS-7375 / GFH375, KRAS G12D(ON/OFF)-selective inhibitor + cetuximab — 1L cohort (NCT07644559)
picks.rationale: VS-7375 gives a fourth front-line-eligible G12D-selective slot: NCT07644559 has a 1L cohort admitting treatment-naive patients at ECOG 1, and the monotherapy read was presented at ESMO 2025 (LBA84) in previously treated G12D PDAC at ORR 41% (90% CI 30-52), doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.09.099. That Western congress presentation and the US sponsor keep it inside the guideline-consonant, trial-enrollment frame under NCCN Pancreatic v2.2025 rather than resting on non-Western data alone. It ranks below the phase-3-anchored options because its own controlled evidence is a phase 3 that sits at second line (NCT07262567), not first.
primary_concerns: The 1L cohort is phase 2 single-arm; the randomized read (NCT07262567) is second-line and still recruiting.
Cetuximab adds a rash/hypomagnesemia burden that the single-agent RAS(ON) trials do not carry.
The efficacy anchor is a China-based phase 1/2 (GFH375X1101); enrollment should confirm the US cohort's line and ECOG fit before relying on it.

picks.intervention_label: ceralasertib (AZD6738), ATR inhibitor — ARID1A/BAF250a-stratified basket (NCT03682289)
picks.rationale: His ARID1A frameshift is a real secondary axis, and NCT03682289 assigns treatment by ARID1A/BAF250a status while accepting pancreatic cancer, so it is a trial-enrollment option consonant with NCCN Pancreatic v2.2025 for a pretreated patient once the KRAS-directed slots are exhausted. There is no consensus category, and the clinical read is honest about its limits: the phase-2 signal concentrated in gynecologic histologies with a weak non-gynecologic showing (ORR 14% overall, pmid:41686845). Entry turns on BAF250a loss by IHC, which only about two-thirds of ARID1A-mutant tumors show, so the frameshift alone does not confirm eligibility.
primary_concerns: No PDAC responder in the reported data; the pancreatic signal rests on cross-tumor extrapolation.
BAF250a IHC is the real gate, and it has not been done — a plausible screen-fail.
This is a later-line consideration, not a first move while front-line G12D trials are open.

notes: Re-run over the full current option set (16 prior + 9 new on-axis KRAS/pan-KRAS/vaccine/ATR trial rows). Guideline anchor: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2025 has no consensus category for any KRAS G12D-directed agent because none is FDA-approved; the guideline foregrounds comprehensive somatic/germline profiling and clinical-trial enrollment, which is exactly the frame for this whole ranking. Germline-negative on Tempus xG closes the BRCA/PALB2 route, so the olaparib POLO maintenance (category 2A) rationale does not apply here. MSS + TMB 8.6 keeps single-agent checkpoint blockade off the tumor-agnostic label; MMR IHC is the validation gate before any dMMR/MSI-H claim, and I did not rank any checkpoint monotherapy. Ranked front-line-eligible G12D trials by strength of controlled evidence and line-fit: daraxonrasib (phase-3-anchored, breakthrough designation) > zoldonrasib and INCB161734 (front-line phase 3 with phase-1 signal) > VS-7375 (1L phase-2 slot, ESMO-presented). I deliberately did not rank the Hengrui HRS-4642 1L phase 3 (NCT07232875) despite its ORR 63.3% front-line combination read, since its evidence base is a China-based program and its front-line slot pairs with a full gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone; a US patient's guideline-consonant path runs through the Western-sponsored front-line trials first. Pan-KRAS first-in-human agents (BBO-11818, BLU-924), the mRNA/peptide vaccines (ABO2102, SPL mKRASvax), and ELI-002 either lack any efficacy read or match only the adjuvant/maintenance setting, so none clears the bar for a ranked pick. HLA gate honored: C*05:01/C*06:02, not C*08:02, so NT-112 and AZD0240 TCR-T are ineligible and not ranked. Assumes ECOG 1 and treatment-naive per intake; re-rank if performance status or goals-of-care shift, since several front-line slots use mFOLFIRINOX backbones that a more toxicity-averse weighting would push down.

picks.intervention_label: GFH375 / VS-7375, oral KRAS G12D(ON/OFF)-selective inhibitor
picks.rationale: This is the pick that best serves what the patient actually stated. prefers_trials is the one preference carrying weight, and GFH375 has a recruiting first-line PDAC cohort he can enter now (NCT07644559 admits treatment-naive G12D PDAC at ECOG 1), so the door a trials-leaning patient wants is open. It is allele-matched to his exact KRAS G12D, oral, and the ORR of 41% (90% CI 30-52) in previously-treated G12D PDAC is the strongest single-agent response on his own driver anywhere in this dossier. With no toxicity_veto and no modality_constraint to hold against it, the only thing I flag for a 79-year-old is the myelosuppression (grade >=3 neutropenia 8%, anemia 8%) that sits behind the 30% grade >=3 TRAE rate.
primary_concerns: prefers_trials, the KRAS G12D axis, and the oral modality are all satisfied cleanly; the neutral 0.5 weight is the only soft spot, and the free_text itself warns 0.5 may understate how toxicity-averse a 79-year-old is

the 41% ORR read comes from a mostly >=2-prior-line population (68% had >=2 prior lines); the 1L cohort pairs the drug with cetuximab, and that combination's tolerability at his age is not separately reported

picks.intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor
picks.rationale: For a patient who wants a trial, this is the option with the most under it: the only randomized phase 3 evidence on his driver (RASolute 302, OS HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.30-0.53), and a recruiting front-line slot he qualifies for in RASolute 303 (NCT07491445 takes treatment-naive metastatic PDAC and accepts his G12D under its RAS-mutant criterion). It is oral, which costs him nothing under a silent modality field but is worth naming at 79, and pan-RAS covers G12D so it speaks to the lead driver. I put it second rather than first only because GFH375 gives him a G12D-selective agent with a higher on-axis ORR at the same open-1L-trial bar; on evidence depth daraxonrasib is the stronger anchor.
primary_concerns: prefers_trials and oral modality both met; the registration safety read is from 2L, so a longer front-line course of rash (grade >=3 14%) and stomatitis (12%) in a 79-year-old is not yet characterized at 1L
the 1L benefit rests on RASolute 303, which has not read out; the OS HR 0.40 is a 2L number the patient's line does not yet own

picks.intervention_label: zoldonrasib (RMC-9805), KRAS G12D(ON)-selective inhibitor
picks.rationale: If I weight for the man rather than the depth of the data, this is the gentlest agent on his exact allele: at 1200 mg/day no grade 4 or 5 treatment-related events, and the common toxicities were grade 1-2 GI (nausea 27%, diarrhea 20%, vomiting 15%, rash 10%). The free_text flags that a 79-year-old likely warrants more toxicity-aversion than the neutral 0.5 allows me to encode, and this tolerability profile is exactly what that unstated preference would reward. prefers_trials is honored: RASolute 305 (NCT07621718) requires KRAS G12D and is recruiting at first line. It sits behind the two agents above because the base is a single-arm phase 1 of n=40 with no CI on the 30% ORR and no mature PFS, so I cannot tell him how durable it is.
primary_concerns: cleanest tolerability in the set, which is what I would lead with for an older patient, but the neutral 0.5 weight does not formally let me upweight it over the better-evidenced GFH375 and daraxonrasib
the recruiting 1L trial adds chemotherapy to zoldonrasib and the combination toxicity table is not published, so additive myelosuppression at 79 is unquantified

picks.intervention_label: HRS-4642 (KRAS G12D inhibitor) + gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel
picks.rationale: I am surfacing this because it carries the highest front-line response signal on his driver in the whole dossier, a confirmed 63.3% ORR (95% CI 43.9-80.1) in treatment-naive G12D PDAC, and the phase 3 (NCT07232875) matches him on allele, tumor type, and 1L. But I rank it fourth and I am plain about why, because this is where I carry the patient's interests rather than the headline number. The regimen is IV, not oral, and the grade >=3 TRAE rate is 90.3% driven by the gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone, which is a lot of hematologic toxicity to put on a 79-year-old whose free_text already hints he may want a gentler course. And prefers_trials is only half-served here: the phase 3 is not yet recruiting, so the door is not currently open.
primary_concerns: highest 1L ORR on his allele, but IV rather than oral and a 90.3% grade >=3 TRAE burden from the chemo backbone cut against a 79-year-old; with modality_constraints empty I cannot veto on route, only flag it
the enrollable phase 3 is not yet recruiting, so prefers_trials is not fully met today; mPFS/mOS from the phase 1b/2 are still immature

picks.intervention_label: INCB161734, KRAS G12D-selective inhibitor
picks.rationale: This has a strong single-agent signal on his driver, 37% ORR and 78% disease control, and as monotherapy the GI toxicity stayed grade 1-2 with rash and stomatitis notably absent, which is a good fit for an older patient. prefers_trials is served: DAWN-303 (NCT07522073) requires KRAS G12D and enrolls previously untreated metastatic PDAC, and the phase 1 parent (NCT06179160) takes him at his line too, both oral. It lands at rank 5 only because the recruiting front-line trial reads out as inhibitor-plus-chemotherapy, and grade 3 or worse neutropenia clustered near 40% in that combination cohort, which is the number I would put in front of him before he chose this over the cleaner zoldonrasib route.
primary_concerns: prefers_trials and oral modality both met, but the recruiting 1L arm bundles chemotherapy and ~40% grade >=3 neutropenia in that cohort works against a 79-year-old the neutral weight does not protect
the 37% ORR comes from heavily pretreated patients (all >=2 prior lines); mPFS and mDoR are immature, so first-line durability is unproven

picks.intervention_label: ELI-002 2P, lymph-node-targeted amphiphile mKRAS peptide vaccine (G12D/G12R)
picks.rationale: I keep a KRAS vaccine on the list deliberately, because the immunotherapy axis is full of HLA traps and this is the one that does not spring on him. The published anti-KRAS-G12D TCR-T is HLA-C*08:02-restricted and he is C*05:01/C*06:02, so that product cannot present his epitope at all; the NT-112 and A*11:01 TCR-T arms and the A*11:01/C*08:02 mRNA vaccine gate him out on the same genotype. ELI-002 is HLA-agnostic, so his class I type does not exclude it, and its safety is the cleanest thing in the case: no grade 3 or worse treatment-related events across 25 patients. The honest problem is the setting, since the data come from resected minimal-residual-disease PDAC and he has a large primary with liver mets, so I rank it here as a trials-forward option to keep on the table, not a regimen I would put first.
primary_concerns: clears every HLA gate where the C*08:02-restricted TCR-T and A*11:01 programs fail, and the toxicity is the lowest in the dossier, both of which suit the patient; but the MRD/adjuvant evidence does not transfer to bulky metastatic disease
the efficacy split is by on-treatment immune response, not randomization, so it anchors the vaccine mechanism rather than a metastatic benefit estimate

notes: Fresh round-1 re-run over the full current option set, including the 9 newly-added on-axis KRAS trials. The preference file is effectively empty on the axes I usually fight over: toxicity_vetoes [], modality_constraints [], weight a neutral 0.5. So there is no veto to defend and no oral-only line to hold, and the single preference carrying weight is prefers_trials=true. The new evidence changes my top of the ranking versus the prior run: GFH375/VS-7375 now leads because it pairs a 41% ORR on his exact G12D allele with an open, recruiting 1L PDAC cohort (NCT07644559), which is the cleanest marriage of the KRAS driver, prefers_trials, and the oral modality. HRS-4642 + gem/nab-paclitaxel has the highest 1L ORR at 63.3% but I hold it at rank 4 on the patient's behalf: it is IV and its 90.3% grade >=3 TRAE backbone is heavy for a 79-year-old, and its phase 3 is not yet recruiting, so prefers_trials is only half-served. I flag the one tension the case author already named in free_text: the neutral 0.5 understates how toxicity-averse a 79-year-old probably is, which would push zoldonrasib's tolerability up and pull HRS-4642's chemo-combination and INCB161734's neutropenia down if a real preference were captured. On the immunotherapy axis I am holding the line for him: the C*08:02-restricted TCR-T (NT-112), the A*11:01 TCR-T (AZD0240), and the A*11:01/C*08:02 mRNA vaccine are all HLA-excluded for his A*01:01/A*02:01/C*05:01/C*06:02 genotype, so I will not let them be surfaced as live options; only the HLA-agnostic ELI-002 vaccine survives, and it sits low because its evidence is adjuvant/MRD, not metastatic. Checkpoint monotherapy stays off my list given MSS, TMB 8.6, and the single somatic MLH1 variant that most likely reflects MMR-proficient biology; MMR IHC is the gate before anyone claims the dMMR/MSI-H pembrolizumab label. ARID1A/ATR (ceralasertib) drops off this six-pick list once the KRAS field is this deep: it needs BAF250a IHC to gate entry, has no PDAC responder, and its lead basket is not recruiting, so it serves prefers_trials worse than any KRAS option above. ECOG 1 assumed per the case default.
